title: Chilli Cheese Fries
subtitle: Crispy fries with beef chilli and melted cheddar sauce
excerpt: Oven-baked fries piled with Tex-Mex beef chilli and a warm cheddar sauce, served with soured cream and jalapeños. A substantial American diner dish that makes a full meal.
sourceNotes: Chilli cheese fries: an American diner classic, developed in the US from the 1970s onwards as a substantial side dish or meal. Popular across American fast food and diner culture. Based on classic American fast-food and diner published sources.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The chilli can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated. Reheat before serving. Make the fries and cheese sauce fresh.

content.text: Chilli cheese fries are a substantial dish: crispy oven-baked fries under a beef chilli and a warm cheese sauce, finished with soured cream and jalapeños. All three components need to be ready at the same time. Start the chilli first as it needs the longest cook; make the fries while the chilli simmers; make the cheese sauce in the last 10 minutes. Keep the chilli thick and not too saucy. Wet chilli makes the fries soggy fast.

items.prepNote: about 4 medium potatoes, cut into 1 cm sticks
half a tin, drained and rinsed

content.text: Heat {{vegetable-oil}} of oil in a frying pan over medium-high heat. Cook {{onion}} of finely chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add {{beef-mince}} of beef mince and break up as it browns. Add {{garlic}} of crushed garlic, the chilli powder, and cumin. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tinned tomatoes and drained kidney beans. Stir and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes until thick. Season with salt. The chilli must be thick, not runny.

While the chilli simmers, heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potato sticks with the oil, smoked paprika, and salt. Spread in a single layer across two baking trays. Bake for 35-40 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp.
Make the cheese sauce and assemble

Melt the butter in a small pan. Stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes. Add the milk gradually, stirring until smooth. Cook for 3-4 minutes until thickened. Off the heat, stir in the grated cheddar. Season with salt.
Pile the hot fries onto a large plate or tray. Spoon the chilli over the top, then pour the cheese sauce over everything. Scatter soured cream, jalapeños, and spring onion on top. Serve immediately.

items.cause: Chilli too wet, or fries not properly crisp before topping
items.fix: Cook the chilli until very thick. It should hold its shape on a spoon. Make sure the fries are properly crisp and golden before anything goes on top.
The chilli is the longest element (25-30 mins total). Start it first. Put the fries in 15 minutes after the chilli, so both finish around the same time. Make the cheese sauce in the last 10 minutes.

items.symptom: Chilli is too wet and pooling
items.fix: Simmer the chilli uncovered. If still too wet, mash some of the kidney beans into the chilli to thicken it without adding more flour.

items.cause: Spices not cooked in the fat
items.fix: Add the chilli powder and cumin directly to the browned mince and cook for 2 minutes before adding any liquid. Spices need fat and heat to bloom.

content.text: Chilli cheese fries are a classic American diner and fast food order: a side dish that became a meal by adding a beef chilli topping to an already generous cheese fries. They're deeply associated with American comfort food culture and appear on menus from highway diners to sports bars. In Britain, the dish arrived with the American casual dining wave of the 2010s and has become a pub menu fixture.
